name: M.Sc. (Horticulture) Vegetable Science
duration_note: Coursework generally comes in the first year and thesis research in the second. The ICAR BSMA master's framework totals 70 credits, including 30 credits of thesis research.
regulator: ICAR (Broad Subject Matter Area PG syllabi, Horticultural Sciences)

hero.summary: A two-year research master's in olericulture that covers breeding, seed production, protected cultivation and production systems for cool- and warm-season vegetables. Students pair advanced coursework with a supervised thesis, building skills for research, seed industry, state horticulture and high-value vegetable enterprises.

overview.heading: Inside the Vegetable Science master's
paragraphs: M.Sc. (Horticulture) Vegetable Science, also listed as Olericulture, focuses on vegetable crops from variety development to the market. Students study how cool-season and warm-season vegetables are grown, how self- and cross-pollinated crops are bred, how hybrid and open-pollinated seed is produced, and how polyhouses, shade nets and soilless systems change production.

Most agricultural and horticultural universities base the programme on the ICAR Broad Subject Matter Area (BSMA) PG syllabus for Horticultural Sciences, adapted locally. Students take major courses in vegetable science, minor and supporting courses from other departments, common courses and a seminar, and then complete a thesis. Tamil Nadu Agricultural University describes coursework followed by 30 credits of thesis research.

The degree is widely available. TNAU offers it at its Coimbatore and Periyakulam horticulture colleges, and Dr YSP University of Horticulture and Forestry lists it at Nauni and Neri. Research themes follow local conditions, for example off-season and temperate vegetable seed production in hill regions or tropical vegetables and protected cultivation in the plains.

highlights.label: Credit structure (ICAR BSMA)
highlights.value: 70 credits: major 20, minor 8, supporting 6, common 5, seminar 1, thesis 30

who_should_apply: Horticulture or agriculture graduates drawn to vegetable breeding, hybrid development and seed technology.
Students curious about polyhouse, net-house and hydroponic production of high-value vegetables.
Applicants planning research, teaching or seed-industry careers who can commit to a field or lab thesis.
Those interested in starting or advising vegetable nurseries, seed production or protected-cultivation ventures.

curriculum.heading: Courses, research and field work
curriculum.intro: Universities draw their course lists from the ICAR BSMA Horticultural Sciences syllabus, but titles, codes and electives are set by each university's academic council, so subject names vary. The areas below are representative of vegetable science major courses; minor and supporting courses are agreed with the advisory committee.

structure.focus: Production, improvement and seed systems for vegetable crops.
courses: Growth and development of vegetable crops
Breeding of self- and cross-pollinated vegetable crops
Underutilised, spice and organic vegetable production
Systematics and postharvest management of vegetable crops

structure.focus: Courses from related departments chosen to support the thesis.
courses: Genetics and plant breeding or molecular biology
Plant pathology, entomology or soil science

structure.focus: ICAR-mandated courses on research practice and communication.
courses: Intellectual property and its management in agriculture
Agricultural research, research ethics and rural development programmes

practical_learning.name: Thesis research
practical_learning.description: A supervised study, usually started after first-year coursework, designed with a major adviser and advisory committee and defended in a final viva voce.

practical_learning.name: Field and protected-structure practicals
practical_learning.description: Work in university vegetable fields, polyhouses and seed plots on crop raising, hybridisation and seed handling.

practical_learning.name: Exposure visits and seminars
practical_learning.description: Visits to research stations and seed farms, plus departmental seminars, at universities that schedule them.

points: A four-year bachelor's degree in horticulture is the usual entry qualification; some universities also accept B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture for Vegetable Science. Accepted degrees vary by university and year.
For ICAR AIEEA (PG), Vegetable Science sits in the Horticulture subject group; qualifying degrees and minimum OGPA/percentage by category are set in that year's information bulletin.
Final-year students can usually apply provisionally, provided they finish the degree with the required marks by the admission deadline.
University seats follow their own minimum OGPA, domicile and reservation rules, which differ by state.

routes.name: ICAR AIEEA (PG)
routes.description: National NTA-run test for ICAR's share of master's seats in agricultural universities and for ICAR deemed university seats; rank also governs the ICAR PG scholarship.

routes.name: University PG entrance test
routes.description: Remaining seats are usually filled through the university's own entrance test or merit list. Dr YSPUHF, for example, used PGET scores in the 2023 cycle.

routes.name: Self-financing and other quotas
routes.description: Some universities offer self-financing, sports or in-service seats with separate rules published in the prospectus.

exams.name: ICAR AIEEA (PG)
exams.note: Computer-based test with a Horticulture subject paper; pattern and dates change by year.

exams.name: University PG entrance tests
exams.note: Syllabi and selection weightage vary by university.

steps.title: Check eligibility
steps.text: Match your degree and OGPA against the ICAR bulletin and the prospectus of each target university.

steps.title: Register for entrance tests
steps.text: Apply for ICAR AIEEA (PG) through NTA and for the PG entrance tests of chosen universities.

steps.title: Attend counselling
steps.text: Use your rank in ICAR online counselling or university counselling to select subject and institution.

steps.title: Complete admission
steps.text: Report with original documents and pay fees at the allotted university before the deadline.

fees.summary: Fees vary with the university and seat type. Regular seats at state agricultural and horticultural universities usually cost less than self-financing seats, and ICAR-quota, state-quota and non-resident fees may be set differently. Hostel, mess and examination charges are extra. No figures are listed because no dated official fee schedule was verified; check the current prospectus.

careers.heading: Career directions after Vegetable Science
careers.intro: The degree supports careers in public horticulture, research and the vegetable seed and production industry. Many graduates continue to a Ph.D. or prepare for national eligibility and scientist recruitment tests. Recruitment rules differ by employer and state, and selection is competitive.

roles.title: Horticulture officer / assistant director of horticulture
roles.description: Runs state horticulture schemes and grower support programmes; TNAU lists this among career options for its graduates.

roles.title: Subject matter specialist (horticulture) at a KVK
roles.description: Conducts trials, demonstrations and farmer training on vegetable production.

roles.title: Vegetable breeder or seed production executive
roles.description: Works on variety and hybrid development or seed multiplication in private seed companies.

roles.title: Research fellow or associate
roles.description: Supports funded vegetable research projects in universities and ICAR institutes.

roles.title: Protected-cultivation entrepreneur or farm manager
roles.description: Manages polyhouse, net-house or hydroponic production of high-value vegetables.

public_sector_routes: ICAR ASRB National Eligibility Test (NET) in Vegetable Science for lecturer/assistant professor eligibility
ICAR ASRB Agricultural Research Service and related scientist recruitment
State public service commission horticulture officer examinations
higher_study: Ph.D. in Vegetable Science (via ICAR AICE-JRF/SRF (PhD) or university entrance)
Ph.D. in seed science and technology or related disciplines, subject to university rules

skills: Field experiment design and statistical analysis

faqs.question: Who is eligible for M.Sc. Vegetable Science?
faqs.answer: Horticulture graduates are the main intake, and some universities also accept B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture. The exact degree list and minimum OGPA are published in the ICAR AIEEA (PG) bulletin and each university's prospectus.

faqs.question: How do I get admission?
faqs.answer: Through ICAR AIEEA (PG), run by NTA, for ICAR-quota and ICAR deemed university seats, or through the university's own PG entrance or merit process for its remaining seats.

faqs.question: Is Vegetable Science the same as Olericulture?
faqs.answer: Yes. Olericulture is the traditional name, and ICAR notices often list the subject as 'Vegetable Science / Olericulture'.

faqs.question: What does the coursework include?
faqs.answer: Production of cool- and warm-season vegetables, vegetable breeding, seed production and protected cultivation are typical major areas, supported by statistics and related subjects. Titles vary by university.

faqs.question: How much of the degree is research?
faqs.answer: In the ICAR BSMA framework, 30 of the 70 credits go to thesis research, normally carried out in the second year under an adviser.

faqs.question: What jobs suit Vegetable Science graduates?
faqs.answer: Options include state horticulture posts, KVK subject matter specialist roles, breeder or seed roles in private companies, research fellowships and protected-cultivation enterprises.

faqs.question: Can I pursue a Ph.D. afterwards?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ph.D. admission is through ICAR AICE-JRF/SRF (PhD) or university entrance tests, and Vegetable Science is also an ASRB NET discipline for teaching eligibility.
